page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture and virtualized via KVM, it features 16 physical cores configured with 2 threads per core, yielding 32 vCPUs. System memory totals 64 GB, providing 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes no local storage and relies on external disk options, supported by a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Performance data reveals a noticeable distinction between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core benchmarks rank in the lower performance quartile, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 963 and weak gzip compression rates. Conversely, multi-threaded tasks scale effectively across the 32 vCPUs, achieving average performance levels with a PassMark CPU score of 23,057.96 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 23,528.93.

In operational benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates consistent middle-tier output for web and data workloads. It handles 23.22 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 13.98 GB/sec. Given its hardware density and performance profile, ecs.sn1ne.8xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallel applications, microservice host nodes, and batch compute pipelines that do not depend on high single-thread speeds.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance equipped with 32 vCPUs across 16 physical Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 64 GB of RAM. Running under KVM virtualization, this x86_64 server provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps and includes no local instance storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight a clear tradeoff between single-threaded and parallel performance: while single-core execution scores in the lower quartile across tests like Geekbench and gzip, multi-core scaling reaches middle-tier levels with strong results in PassMark and multi-threaded decompression tests. The 2:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio delivers compute density for parallel tasks, enabling 23.22 million Redis SET operations per second and stable web serving throughput. Overall, ecs.sn1ne.8xlarge fits highly parallel application servers, microservice clusters, and batch computing tasks that prioritize core count over individual thread frequency.
